summary: This is an adapted simulation using EV6 processor with GCC power trace in HotSpot, not a reproduction of the paper's Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) study. The paper presents a 3D finite element model (FEniCS) with Galerkin projection using pulsed power at three functional units (A, B, C) on a 129×129×7 mesh, achieving model reduction by >4 orders of magnitude. The current simulation uses HotSpot's steady-state and transient thermal analysis on an EV6 floorplan with fixed power trace, producing block-level and grid-level temperatures. While both concern CPU thermal simulation, they employ fundamentally different methodologies (POD/FEniCS vs. HotSpot RC network), different workload patterns (pulsed vs. GCC trace), and different thermal modeling assumptions. No numerical correspondence should be expected between POD reduced-order results and HotSpot block temperatures.
limitations: No 3D geometry or mesh matching the paper's structure
Power input is a GCC benchmark trace, not the pulsed 3.333μs period used in the paper
HotSpot uses lumped RC thermal network, not FEniCS 3D PDE solver
No POD or Galerkin projection implemented; steady-state and basic transient analysis only
Boundary conditions differ: HotSpot uses fixed ambient, paper specifies Robin conditions with 0°C ambient
Thermal material properties (conductivity, density, heat capacity) not validated against paper values
Paper reports model reduction comparison (3 vs. 5 POD modes vs. FEniCS reference); this run outputs absolute temperatures without reduction metrics
Different processor architectures at functional unit level: HotSpot floorplan blocks versus paper's idealized A, B, C functional units
